Triage: `pm:queue` · Bug — a public exported props interface still invites the rc.6-retired `{ key, defaultValue }` label form (objectstack#5055), and the runtime paints the raw dotted key with property-order-dependent behavior; the sibling `MetricWidgetProps` was already migrated for exactly this reason (#4358). Fix: migrate the four members to `string | I18nLabel`, plus the same-pass fixture sweep the card names (#4032 fixture-triage discipline: a fixture pinning the retired branch keeps passing precisely because nothing produces it any more).

## Correction: my Clause-② framing was backwards, and tsc says so

I would have classified this migration as a **narrowing** — retiring `{ key, defaultValue }` in favour of `string | I18nLabel` reads like removing an accepted form. The dev measured it instead of accepting the framing, and it is not a narrowing:

`I18nLabel`'s object half erases to `Record<string, string>` in the emitted `.d.ts`. The BCP-47 key regex is a **Zod runtime refinement that does not survive into the type**. So `{ key, defaultValue }` **remains structurally assignable** — nothing about this change stops it type-checking.

What *starts* type-checking is the **inline per-locale map**, which the old declaration rejected with TS2353. Stated plainly:

> **A consumer writing the only vocabulary the spec admits previously could not compile.**

So the accept set on the type axis **widens, toward the contract** — the opposite of what "retire the old form" suggests. The retired form is refused where refusal is actually expressible: `I18nLabelSchema` rejects it at authoring time in **both property orders**, now pinned in tests.

Recording it because the wrong framing was mine and it was published in the dispatch order.

## The reader fix is the part users would have noticed

`drawerTitle` destructured `title?.defaultValue` / `label?.defaultValue` — a limb an inline locale map does not have. An authored drill-down title therefore resolved to `''` and the panel silently fell back to the literal word **"Details"**. Both reads now go through `pickLocalized` against the same UI language the tile uses. A declaration migration that left this reader alone would have type-checked, passed, and still shown the wrong title.

## Escalated, not decided here

The dev's open question is a genuine fork and it is **not** this seat's to settle: TypeScript cannot express the rejection of `{ key, defaultValue }` on **any** `I18nLabel` surface in **either** repo, because `InlineLocaleMapSchema` is `z.record(z.string().regex(BCP47), z.string())` and the key regex is erased — every string key type-checks.

That is a `@objectstack/spec` contract change, so it goes to the spec seat's queue and the maintainer's inbox rather than being answered in an objectui PR. Filed as **objectstack-ai/objectstack#9925**. Its recommendation (narrow the key to a template-literal/branded locale-tag type) is carried across with the dev's own reasoning, including the cost it names — computed keys may need an escape hatch, which is exactly why it is a maintainer call.

## Two more things worth keeping

**Reverse verification named a missed prediction rather than rounding it off.** Predicted 3 RED / 9 GREEN in vitest, observed exactly that — the failure text reproduces the issue's own measurement verbatim (`expected 'crm.dashboards.sales.widgets.revenue.…' to contain 'Total Revenue'`). For type-check it predicted RED and observed RED, but predicted error code **TS2353** and observed **TS2322** — same meaning, different code, because the failures land in JSX attribute position rather than a fresh literal binding. It reported the miss.

**The ablation's rebuild analysis is the standard to copy.** The vitest leg has no artifact in the path (`vitest.config.mts` aliases every `@object-ui/*` to that package's `src/`, and the ablated file is reached by a relative import). But the type-check leg's `tsconfig.test.json` sets `"paths": {}`, so `@object-ui/types` resolves through its **built `.d.ts`** — that artifact **is** in the path. It built the dependency closure before reading any measurement, and noted the artifact is unchanged by the ablation either way. Most reports assert "no rebuild needed" globally; this one checked each leg separately and found they differed.

PR #5303 is **not** being flipped to ready: `Build & E2E` is broken repo-wide (#5304, p0) and the maintainer ruled 2026-08-19 「先修 CI,PR 一律等着」.
